h: A prime minister's house and a park to roam
p: The Gordons of Haddo weren't just country gentry. George Hamilton-Gordon, 4th Earl of Aberdeen, served as Prime Minister in the 1850s, during the Crimean War, so this house has links to the very top of Victorian politics. Keep that in mind when you're looking at all those family portraits and you'll start piecing the story together.

Haddo has a musical side too. Haddo Arts has a long tradition of concerts, opera and choral performances, carrying on a family enthusiasm for music that goes back generations. If you like a bit of culture with your history, it's worth seeing what's on before you plan your trip.

Next door, Haddo Country Park is run separately by Aberdeenshire Council and is a big bonus for families and dog walkers. There are lakes, woodland and open parkland to explore, with plenty of space to let the kids run off some energy after the house tour. In autumn the colours through the trees are a real treat.

Give yourself at least half a day to do house and park justice. If you're making a day of it, Pitmedden Garden and the ruins of Tolquhon Castle are both a short drive away. Ellon itself sits on the River Ythan, and following the river towards the coast brings you to Newburgh, where the beach at the river mouth is famous for its big colony of grey seals lounging on the sands. Watch them from across the water and don't disturb them, and you'll have a memorable end to the day.
